arxiv-2111-04012.title: A-PixelHop: A Green, Robust and Explainable Fake-Image Detector
arxiv-2111-04012.creator: Yao Zhu, Xinyu Wang, Hong-Shuo Chen, Ronald Salloum, C.-C. Jay Kuo
arxiv-2111-04012.description: Abstract A novel method for detecting CNN-generated images, called Attentive PixelHop (or A-PixelHop), is proposed in this work. It has three advantages: 1) low computational complexity and a small model size, 2) high detection performance against a wide range of generative models, and 3) mathematical transparency.

arxiv-2306-00717.description: Abstract Recently, deep neural networks have emerged as a solution to solve NP-hard wireless resource allocation problems in real-time. However, multi-layer perceptron (MLP) and convolutional neural network (CNN) structures, which are inherited from image processing tasks, are not optimized for wireless network problems. As network size increases, these methods get harder to train and generalize.

arxiv-2403-03462.creator: Ali Ayub, Chrystopher L. Nehaniv, Kerstin Dautenhahn
arxiv-2403-03462.description: Abstract For robots to perform assistive tasks in unstructured home environments, they must learn and reason on the semantic knowledge of the environments. Despite a resurgence in the development of semantic reasoning architectures, these methods assume that all the training data is available a priori.

arxiv-2409-03730.title: Likelihood Geometry of the Squared Grassmannian
arxiv-2409-03730.creator: Hannah Friedman
arxiv-2409-03730.description: Abstract We study projection determinantal point processes and their connection to the squared Grassmannian. We prove that the log-likelihood function of this statistical model has ( n − 1 ) ! / 2 (n-1)!/2 critical points, all of which are real and positive, thereby settling a conjecture of Devriendt, Friedman, Reinke, and Sturmfels. † † MSC2020: 62R01, 14M15, 14P25.

arxiv-2505-24130.title: Instantons and topological order in two-leg electron ladders: A universality class
arxiv-2505-24130.creator: S.-R. Eric Yang, Hyun Cheol Lee, Hoang-Anh Le, In-Hwan Lee
arxiv-2505-24130.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by S.-R. Eric Yang, Hyun Cheol Lee, Hoang-Anh Le, In-Hwan Lee. Our numerical study of the disordered Hubbard model with nearest-neighbor hopping shows that a two-leg electron ladder has a finite topological entanglement entropy in the regime where the density of states exhibits an exponentially decaying gap. The value of the topological entanglement entropy suggests that two-leg ladders belong to the same universality class as graphene zigzag nanoribbons, despite several structural differences.

arxiv-2509-00796.title: In-plane transverse polarization in heavy-ion collisions
arxiv-2509-00796.creator: Anum Arslan, Wen-Bo Dong, Charles Gale, Sangyong Jeon, Qun Wang, Xiang-Yu Wu
arxiv-2509-00796.description: Abstract We give an analytical expression for the last component of the spin polarization P x P^{x} , the in-plane polarization, in heavy-ion collisions that has, to our knowledge, not been discussed in theories nor measured in heavy-ion collision experiments.

pmc-10714644.title: Role of IL-33-ST2 pathway in regulating inflammation: current evidence and future perspectives
pmc-10714644.creator: Yilu Zhou, Zhendong Xu, Zhiqiang Liu
pmc-10714644.description: Interleukin (IL)-33 is an alarmin of the IL-1 superfamily localized to the nucleus of expressing cells, such as endothelial cells, epithelial cells, and fibroblasts. In response to cellular damage or stress, IL-33 is released and activates innate immune responses in some immune and structural cells via its receptor interleukin-1 receptor like-1 (IL-1RL1 or ST2).

pmc-11320628.title: Breakfast Skipping and Determinant Factors among Moroccan School Adolescents (12–19 Years): The Case of Beni Mellal City
pmc-11320628.creator: Kamal Kaoutar, Ahmed Chetoui, Kaltoum Boutahar, Soufiane El Moussaoui, Abdeslam El Kardoudi, Mohamed Najimi, Fatiha Chigr
pmc-11320628.description: IntroductionBreakfast skipping is an unhealthy eating behavior reportedly common among adolescents. The aim of the present study was to determine the prevalence and factors associated with breakfast skipping among schoolchildren aged 12–19 years in Beni Mellal city, Morocco, and to assist in the design of interventions to improve breakfast consumption habits of school-aged children in this region.

pmc-11492916.title: Cytotoxic Evaluation, Molecular Docking, Molecular Dynamics, and ADMET Prediction of Isolupalbigenin Isolated from Erythrina subumbrans (Hassk). Merr. (Fabaceae) Stem Bark: Unveiling Its Anticancer Efficacy

In our ongoing research on folk medical plants, we report the isolation of flavonoid compound from the stem bark of E.

pmc-11516270.title: 6.E. Practice session: Using European environmental data in public health: datasets and applications
pmc-11516270.creator: Organised by: European Environment Agency, Chair persons: Gerardo Sanchez Martinez (Denmark)
pmc-11516270.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The European Environment Agency collects, quality-assures and quality-checks data on environment, climate and sustainability. It does so through its network and other institutional partners across 38 European countries. Most of these validated environmental data are publicly available and many can be used by practitioners to assess environmental risks to the health of their communities, as well as for designing and evaluating policies’ effectiveness.

pmc-11517022.title: Collection and use of patient-reported experience measures: approach to improve health care
pmc-11517022.creator: I Zile-Velika, V Mavcutko, E Cudina, I Liepina, I Gavare

pmc-11657922.title: Extending the Calgary Audit and Feedback Framework into the virtual environment: a process evaluation and empiric evidence
pmc-11657922.creator: Douglas Woodhouse, Diane Duncan, Leah Ferrie, Onyebuchi Omodon, Ashi Mehta, Surakshya Pokharel, Anshula Ambasta
pmc-11657922.description: BackgroundThe Calgary Audit and Feedback Framework (CAFF) is a pragmatic, evidence-based approach for the design and implementation of in-person social learning interventions using Audit and Group Feedback (AGF). This report describes extension of CAFF into the virtual environment as part of a multifaceted intervention bundle to reduce redundant daily laboratory testing in hospitals.

pmc-11734012.title: Cryoneurolysis and Quadriplegia: A Case Report on Pain and Severe Spasticity Management
pmc-11734012.creator: Laura Schatz, Samuel Herzog, Mahdis Hashemi, Paul Winston
pmc-11734012.description: Spasticity, a common symptom after spinal cord injury, often leads to pain, muscle contracture, and compromised daily activities. Cryoneurolysis, a minimally invasive, drug-free procedure for the treatment of pain, is now gaining recognition for treating spasticity. It involves using an ultrasound-guided probe to freeze and destroy overactive target nerves.

pmc-12520081.title: Personalized Combined Nutrition & Exercise Intervention in Newly Diagnosed Cancer Patients - a Trial Protocol
pmc-12520081.creator: Sebastian Theurich, Timo Niels, Hansjoerg Baurecht, Christine Welker, Annika Tomanek, Ingo Schmidt-Wolf, Christine Greil, Kim Luley, Dirk Forstmeyer, Patrick Jahn, Johann Ockenga, Wibke Jensen, Katharina Graf, Joachim Wiskemann, Caterina Fiorentini, Nora Zoth, Michael Leitzmann, Freerk T Baumann
pmc-12520081.description: The prevalences of malnutrition and sarcopenia are high already at the time of cancer diagnosis and significantly impact on treatment outcomes. Here, we present the protocol of a multicenter, randomized controlled trial to evaluate the efficacy of personalized, combined nutrition and physical exercise interventions in parallel to first-line cancer treatment.

pmc-12550994.title: A Prospective Observational Study to Determine the Efficacy of a Theatre Prioritisation Tool in Optimal Utilisation of Limited Theatre Time for Deep Burn Injury in a Resource-Restricted Setting
pmc-12550994.creator: Nikki Leigh Allorto, Reitze Rodseth, David Gray Bishop
pmc-12550994.description: Background: Routine early surgery for all deep burns in low-resource settings is not currently achievable. We designed and implemented a simple triage strategy that selected patients to be prioritised for early surgery based on a more urgent need and greater potential benefit.

pmc-13074583.title: Interfacial Phenomena of Cotton/Polyester Blended Fabric Modified with Enzyme and Chitosan
pmc-13074583.creator: Anita Tarbuk, Ana Marija Grancarić, Stefana Begović, Tihana Dekanić
pmc-13074583.description: In this study, the interfacial phenomena of cotton/polyester blended fabric modified with enzymes and chitosan were investigated. Enzymatic pretreatments (bioactivation) were carried out using a pectinase complex (Biosol PRO), an esterase complex (Texazym PES), and a combination of both. Bioactivation aimed to activate the surface and improve interfacial properties, primarily the hydrophilicity of the polyester component in the blend.

pmc-13144792.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1522 SIMULTANEOUS STROKE AND STEMI: NAVIGATING A DUAL EMERGENCY IN THE ABSENCE OF GUIDELINES – A CASE SERIES AND LITERATURE REVIEW
pmc-13144792.creator: Veronica Malabet, Juan Tejada, Simona Ivan, Michele Glidden, Marla Doerhing, Nancy Glober, Kristen Quinn, Kyle Frick, Danika Smith, Nicolas Useche
pmc-13144792.description: Background and aimsSimultaneous large vessel occlusion (LVO) cerebral stroke and ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is an unusual but potentially fatal scenario, posing challenges for acute management. The urgent need to reperfuse both the cerebral and coronary vasculatures complicates decision-making in the absence of guidelines to prioritize interventions.

pmc-13156452.title: Modelling Motion‐Induced Signal Corruption in Steady‐State Diffusion MRI
pmc-13156452.creator: Benjamin C Tendler, Wenchuan Wu, Karla L Miller, Aaron T Hess
pmc-13156452.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeDiffusion‐weighted steady‐state free precession (DW‐SSFP) is a diffusion imaging sequence achieving high SNR efficiency. A key challenge for in vivo DW‐SSFP is the sequence's severe motion sensitivity, currently limiting investigations to low or no motion regimes.

pmc-13203161.title: Non-Erythropoietic EPO (EPO-R76E) Protects RPE Cells from Ferroptosis by Modulating the Labile Iron Pool and NRF2-GPX4 Axis †
pmc-13203161.creator: Sundaramoorthy Gopi, George T. Prodanoff, Christopher L. Passaglia, Mark S. Kindy, Vijaykumar Sutariya, Ganesh V. Halade, Alfred S. Lewin, Manas R. Biswal
pmc-13203161.description: Retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) degeneration remains a formidable challenge in dry age-related macular degeneration (AMD) research, primarily due to the toxic interplay between iron overload and ferroptosis. We investigated whether EPO-R76E, a non-erythropoietic modified variant of erythropoietin, could effectively interrupt this destructive cycle.

pmc-13423507.title: Intrapulmonary Bronchogenic Cyst Adjacent to the Inferior Pulmonary Ligament Mimicking a Paraesophageal Mediastinal Cyst: A Case Report
pmc-13423507.creator: Toshiyuki Shima
pmc-13423507.description: Bronchogenic cysts are rare congenital foregut malformations that most commonly arise in the mediastinum. Intrapulmonary bronchogenic cysts are less frequent and may present diagnostic challenges when located adjacent to mediastinal structures. We report a case of an intrapulmonary bronchogenic cyst that closely mimicked a paraesophageal mediastinal cyst on preoperative imaging.

pmc-13586417.title: Ultrasonography in Canine Carpal Disorders
pmc-13586417.creator: Sven Klußmann, Andrea Meyer‐Lindenberg, Andreas Brühschwein
pmc-13586417.description: Ultrasonographic studies of canine carpal disorders are scarce and typically limited to case reports or evaluations of single structures. This prospective, single‐center study characterized ultrasonographic findings in canine carpal disorders confirmed by a composite reference standard and clinical follow‐up, and it assessed the diagnostic role of high‐frequency musculoskeletal ultrasound in relation to radiography and selectively performed cross‐sectional imaging.

pmc-13598788.title: Human metapneumovirus prevention in children: emerging roles of monoclonal antibodies and vaccines
pmc-13598788.creator: Susanna Esposito, Valentina Fainardi, Gaia Giorgia Arnesano, Alberto Argentiero, Nicola Principi
pmc-13598788.description: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a major cause of acute lower respiratory tract infection in children, older adults, and individuals with underlying medical conditions. In pediatric populations, hMPV contributes substantially to hospitalizations, morbidity, and healthcare costs, yet no licensed vaccine or monoclonal antibody is currently available for prevention.

pmc-13632107.title: Prognostic value of admission D-dimer in acute pancreatitis: association with disease severity and clinical outcomes in a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13632107.creator: Elahe Nateghi Baygi, Niloofar Seighali, Mohammad-Sadra Gholami-Chahkand, Morteza Doustmohammadi, Fatemeh Jodeiri, Fahime Salehi
pmc-13632107.description: BackgroundEarly risk stratification in acute pancreatitis (AP) is crucial for improving patient outcomes and guiding timely clinical management. D-dimer has emerged as a potential biomarker reflecting activation of coagulation and fibrinolysis and may assist in early risk stratification of patients with acute pancreatitis. However, its prognostic performance remains incompletely validated across different populations.

pmc-13647598.title: TrLPMO9A drives oxidative cellulose depolymerization in Trichoderma reesei and is enhanced by heterologous cellobiose dehydrogenase expression
pmc-13647598.creator: Priscila Thihara Rodrigues, César Rafael Fanchini Terrasan, Nathalia Rodrigues Bulka, Evandro Antonio de Lima, Jose Alberto Diogo, Renan Yuji Miyamoto, Felipe Jun Fuzita, Joaquim Martins Junior, Lucia Daniela Wolf, Adriano Freitas Lima, Douglas Alvaredo Paixão, Meiski Maria Vedovatto, Lara de Olivei
pmc-13647598.description: BackgroundOne of the most prominent mechanisms for plant cell wall deconstruction in nature, and widely employed in industry, relies on the coordinated action of hydrolytic and oxidative enzymes. However, how redox networks sustain synergistic biomass deconstruction remains incompletely understood, particularly in the industrial workhorse Trichoderma reesei.
